n: A harvest thanksgiving. Praise is waiting for God in Zion, ready to be offered, along with vows made in times of need.

f.g: Some render it “praise is fitting for you” or “silence is praise for you.”

n: God hears prayer, so all people will come to him.
Sins overwhelm us, but God wipes them away. The word “purge” is related to atonement — covering and cleansing sin.

f.g: Atone for, cover — Hebrew kipper, the root of Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement).

n: Blessed is the one God invites close to live in his courts. We will be filled with the good things of his holy temple.
God answers prayers with awesome acts of justice. He is the hope of the whole earth, even distant sailors.
With his power he set the mountains firmly in place.
He calms the roaring seas and the uproar of nations alike — Jesus showed this same power on the Sea of Galilee.

f.w: Which stilleth the noise of the seas

n: People at the ends of the earth stand in awe at God’s signs. From sunrise to sunset, God makes the world sing for joy.

f.w: the outgoings of the morning and evening
f.g: East and west — where the sun rises and sets.

n: God visits the earth with rain. The “river of God” — the rains from heaven — waters the grain fields.

f.g: In KJV English, “corn” means grain such as wheat or barley.

n: He soaks the plowed ridges, levels the furrows, softens the soil with showers, and blesses the sprouts.

f.g: Levels or smooths the plowed rows.

n: God crowns the year with a bountiful harvest; his cart tracks overflow with abundance as he passes.

f.g: Your wagon tracks drip with richness — as a harvest cart spills grain.

n: Even desert pastures receive the overflow, and the hills are wrapped in joy.
Meadows are dressed with flocks and valleys draped in grain — the whole landscape shouts and sings. Creation itself joins the praise.

f.w: they shout for joy, they also sing
